open_points.subject: REGISTRY_BASE_URL startup requiredness and validation
open_points.text: A30 now says “REGISTRY_BASE_URL … is no required start-up variable, and its absence fails only Registry calls,” while R0-10 says “The service is configured only by environment variables, which it validates when it starts,” and A30’s carried configuration says the environment-variable table includes “requiredness” and is “read into RuntimeSettings.”
open_points.question: Is REGISTRY_BASE_URL explicitly exempt from startup environment validation and from the startup RuntimeSettings snapshot, so the service must start when it is absent?
options: REGISTRY_BASE_URL is exempt: startup succeeds without it and later Registry calls fail as transport_error.
R0-10’s startup validation still applies: startup fails when REGISTRY_BASE_URL is absent.
Startup reads the variable into RuntimeSettings but treats absence as valid, leaving unclear whether the gateway reads RuntimeSettings or the environment directly.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the changed A30 rule as a specific exception to R0-10: allow startup without REGISTRY_BASE_URL and fail affected Registry calls as transport_error.

witness.initial: The deployment environment has every otherwise-required setting but REGISTRY_BASE_URL is absent.
events: The host operator starts the portal.
After startup, an authenticated actor invokes an operation that requires Registry validation.
outcomes: Under changed A30 and A6, startup succeeds; the later operation fails with RegistryFailureKind transport_error.
Under R0-10’s unqualified startup-validation rule, startup is refused and no operation can be invoked.
witness.observer: The host operator sees either a running service with a per-call Registry failure or a startup failure.

open_points.subject: REGISTRY_BASE_URL configuration lifetime
open_points.text: A30 now says “REGISTRY_BASE_URL is read by the Registry gateway at each call,” while State 1 names RuntimeSettings and RuntimeEnvironment as “the startup configuration … read from the environment,” and A30 still says config.runtime_environment_variables is “read into RuntimeSettings.”
open_points.question: After startup, does each Registry call observe the current process-environment value of REGISTRY_BASE_URL, or the value captured in startup RuntimeSettings?
options: Read the process environment anew for every Registry call, so runtime changes affect the next call.
Use the startup RuntimeSettings value for the process lifetime.
Refresh or mutate RuntimeSettings before calls, though no such mechanism is specified.
open_points.default_guess: Follow the changed A30 sentence literally and read REGISTRY_BASE_URL from the environment on every Registry call, outside the startup RuntimeSettings snapshot.

witness.initial: The portal starts while REGISTRY_BASE_URL points to Registry A; Registry A and Registry B return distinguishable project contexts for the same project_id.
events: The host operator starts the service.
The process environment value is changed to Registry B without restarting the service.
An authenticated viewer opens the project overview, causing a Registry call.
outcomes: A per-call environment read sends the request to Registry B and the viewer sees B’s context.
A startup RuntimeSettings snapshot sends the request to Registry A and the viewer sees A’s context.
witness.observer: The viewer sees different project context, and the host operator sees a different Registry receive the request.
